clue.text: Untidy hair needs perm as result of explosion

parts.note: a shock is a thick, tousled mass of hair
a perm puts a wave into the hair, so perm can stand for wave

explanation.surface: A hairdresser's warning that a messy mop needs a perm after some blast.
explanation.definitionFit: A blast sends out a surge of pressure through the air, which is the thing named here.

clue.text: Airborne, I hear, will be one following in line

definitions.text: Airborne, I hear, will be one following in line

parts.words: Airborne, I hear, will be one following in line
parts.note: heard aloud, 'air borne' is 'heir born': a newborn heir will one day follow on in the line of succession

explanation.walkthrough: The play is on sound: 'air' said aloud is 'heir', and an heir born will in time take over.
explanation.definitionFit: One who follows another in an office or line of descent is the next holder after them.

clue.text: First of onions has obstinate smell

indicators.note: first of means take only the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: dour can mean stern or obstinate

explanation.surface: The opening whiff of onions has a stubborn pong.
explanation.definitionFit: A smell, especially a distinct or lingering one, is a synonym.

clue.text: Friendly swimmer helps us start a fire

definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for a noun: the material that helps us start a fire

parts.note: kind means friendly
a ling is a sea fish of the cod family, a swimmer

explanation.surface: A friendly fish lends a hand lighting a campfire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swimmer' is a crossword favourite for a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Small sticks and dry twigs used to get a blaze going are called this.

clue.text: Poison with fatal implication for the Greeks

definitions.text: Poison with fatal implication for the Greeks

parts.words: Poison with fatal implication for the Greeks
parts.note: the drug is named after Atropos, the Greek Fate who cuts the thread of life

explanation.walkthrough: Atropos was one of the three Fates of Greek myth, the one who cut each life's thread; the belladonna poison takes its name from her.
explanation.definitionFit: Atropine is a toxic alkaloid from deadly nightshade, named from Atropos, one of the Fates.

clue.text: One angle new to London borough

indicators.note: new here means made afresh, so the letters are put in a fresh order

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A fresh viewpoint on a part of London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges I and ANGLE together. Ealing is a borough in west London.
explanation.definitionFit: Ealing is one of the outer boroughs of Greater London, in the west of the city.

clue.text: Print of Java

parts.note: a printed fabric technique native to the Indonesian island, using wax to resist the dye

explanation.definitionFit: Batik is the wax-resist dyed cloth for which Java is famous, a kind of printed textile.

clue.text: Born irritable and malicious

parts.note: b is the standard abbreviation for born, as in dates
itchy can mean restless or irritated

explanation.surface: A person described as naturally grumpy and spiteful.
explanation.definitionFit: Bitchy is a slang term for spiteful or catty.

clue.text: He causes distress to religious leader and adviser

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, so take the start of religious

parts.note: a mentor is a trusted adviser

explanation.surface: A bully harasses a churchman and his counsellor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'religious leader' looks like a priest or bishop, but 'leader' takes just the R of 'religious'.
explanation.definitionFit: One who torments is a person who inflicts suffering, which is causing distress.

clue.text: Old Russian peasant as king over our kingdom (including the French)

indicators.note: in a down clue over means placed above, so first in the answer

parts.note: K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

indicators.note: including means holding something within, so a container

parts.note: UK is the United Kingdom, our kingdom to a British setter
la is French for the

explanation.surface: A Russian peasant playing king over Britain, with the French involved too.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' means placed above, so the king comes first. Kulaks were the better-off peasants persecuted under Stalin.
explanation.definitionFit: A kulak was a prosperous peasant farmer in Russia before and after the Revolution.

clue.text: In historic speech court official promotes draughtsman

definitions.meaning: an old or dialect word for the officer who holds inquests into deaths
in draughts a piece reaching the far row is crowned, so this is one who crowns a piece

explanation.surface: A court officer, talking in an old-fashioned way, advances a technical drawer.
explanation.walkthrough: Draughts is the British name for checkers; a piece that is promoted is crowned, and the word here is also Shakespeare's form of 'coroner'.
explanation.definitionFit: The old word for a coroner, and literally a person who crowns, as with a promoted piece in checkers.

clue.text: Tear madly into all-out shoot

indicators.note: the clue says one rearranged word goes into the other, so a container
out here means out of order, telling us to rearrange the word all
acting madly means wildly disordered, so the word tear is scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone tears wildly into a full-scale photo shoot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'madly' makes ATER and 'out' makes LAL, and 'into' places the first inside the second after its opening letter. 'Shoot' is the botanical noun, not a photo session.
explanation.definitionFit: In botany a lateral is a side branch growing from the main stem, that is, a sideways sprout.

clue.text: Lenore no end worried, having to register

indicators.note: worried in the sense of disturbed or shaken up, so the letters are rearranged
with no end means the final letter of the name is dropped

explanation.surface: A woman called Lenore frets endlessly about having to sign up for something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no end' drops the last E of LENORE to leave LENOR, which 'worried' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: To enrol is to sign up or put your name on a list, the same as registering.

clue.text: Choose to coat the odd bench with imitation gold

indicators.note: coating something means wrapping round it, so one word surrounds the other

parts.note: to pick is to choose

indicators.note: odd here means strange or out of order, so the word bench is rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone decides to paint a strange bench with fake gilt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' makes NCHBE, and 'to coat' wraps the synonym for choose round it. 'Odd' tempts as a call for alternate letters, but those give only BNH.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinchbeck is a copper and zinc alloy made to look like gold, so it is a fake or sham gilt.

clue.text: What, still no current?

parts.note: reads like a complaint about a power cut, but describes water that is motionless with no flow

explanation.definitionFit: Water that lies still and does not flow is described as stale and motionless, with no movement through it.

clue.text: So-called strong man of 17th century tragedy

definitions.text: So-called strong man of 17th century tragedy

parts.words: So-called strong man of 17th century tragedy
parts.note: points to Milton's Samson tragedy, whose title gives Samson a Greek epithet

explanation.walkthrough: Samson Agonistes (1671) is John Milton's closet tragedy; the standard spelling ends -ES, and the grid's -IS is a slip.
explanation.definitionFit: Milton titled his drama about the biblical strongman with this Greek word, meaning champion or contender.

clue.text: Attempt crazy return

indicators.note: a return goes back the way it came, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: bats is informal for mad or crazy

explanation.surface: A mad tennis return that is really just a try.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' reverses BATS.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a go at something is to have a try at it, an informal synonym.

clue.text: Flower with flatter calyx

parts.note: to butter someone is to flatter them
a calyx is the cup of sepals beneath a flower

explanation.surface: A bloom with a rather flattering cup round its petals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flatter' reads as an adjective (more flat) but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The buttercup is a common yellow meadow plant of the genus Ranunculus.

clue.text: Goose grows attached to Hull

definitions.meaning: the ... goose, a black-and-white Arctic species
a crustacean that fixes itself to the bottom of ships

explanation.surface: A goose takes up residence in the Yorkshire port of Hull.
explanation.walkthrough: Hull is a port city in Yorkshire; the capital H disguises a ship's hull.
explanation.definitionFit: A type of Arctic goose, and also the shelled sea creature that clings to ship bottoms.

clue.text: Treacle left out in sideboard

indicators.note: out here means put out of its proper order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Golden syrup has been left out on the dining-room cabinet.
explanation.walkthrough: Treacle is British for golden syrup or molasses.
explanation.definitionFit: A cellaret is a cabinet or compartment of a sideboard for holding wine bottles.

clue.text: Backdoor clue to crossword?

annotationWithheld.why: Clue 'Backdoor clue to crossword?' (ROOD): the one word 'Backdoor' is both the reversal indicator (Back) and the fodder (door), a word doing two jobs that the check refuses.

clue.text: Strangelove loved, messing about in boats

definitions.text: Strangelove loved, messing about in boats

parts.words: Strangelove loved, messing about in boats
parts.note: recalls the Wind in the Willows character who declares nothing is half so worth doing as pottering in boats

explanation.walkthrough: The Wind in the Willows is Kenneth Grahame's children's book; its riverbank character Ratty says nothing is better than 'simply messing about in boats'.
explanation.definitionFit: The riverbank rodent in Grahame's novel is the animal who famously loves boating more than anything.

clue.text: "A ---- smitten with the morning sun" (Tennyson)

parts.note: a line from Tennyson's The Palace of Art, naming the Egyptian statue said to sing at dawn

explanation.walkthrough: The Colossi of Memnon at Thebes in Egypt were said to make a sound when struck by the rising sun.
explanation.definitionFit: The statue at Egyptian Thebes was believed to sing when the dawn light touched it.

clue.text: Society dressmaker

definitions.meaning: a church group of women who make clothes for the poor
the woman in Acts who sewed garments for widows

explanation.walkthrough: A Dorcas society is a church sewing circle named after the charitable woman in Acts 9.
explanation.definitionFit: The disciple in Acts known for making clothes, after whom charitable sewing circles are named.

clue.text: Eg second generation Brahmin

parts.note: Hindus of the upper castes undergo a sacred-thread ceremony seen as a spiritual second birth

explanation.definitionFit: Hindu castes initiated with the sacred thread, Brahmins above all, are said to be born a second time spiritually.

clue.text: Submit to oral examination with relish

definitions.meaning: to try with the mouth, testing food or drink
relish as in liking or appetite

explanation.surface: A candidate faces a viva and enjoys it.
explanation.definitionFit: To sample food by mouth, and also a liking or appetite for something.

clue.text: Whereat a gentleman is free

parts.note: a gentleman with no fixed occupation is said to be at this, and the phrase also means at liberty

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase 'at large' means free or unconfined, and 'a gentleman at large' is one without settled employment.

clue.text: These lectures have had their form changed

indicators.note: their form changed says the letters of the word are reshaped into a new order

explanation.surface: A lecture series that has been reformatted.
explanation.walkthrough: The Reith Lectures are annual BBC radio talks named after Lord Reith, the BBC's first Director-General.
explanation.definitionFit: The Reith Lectures are the BBC's annual series of radio talks by a leading figure.

clue.text: Blake's mills are devilish dark

parts.note: recalls the poem Jerusalem by William Blake, with its dark mills of the industrial age

explanation.walkthrough: Blake's hymn 'Jerusalem' speaks of 'these dark Satanic mills'; 'devilish' gives the meaning of the missing word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word in Blake's line means fiendish, belonging to the Devil.

clue.text: Hearty character joining 1 ac?

parts.note: a card is an eccentric or amusing character
the numeral one is the Roman letter I
taken as written

explanation.surface: A big-hearted joker linked to the answer at 1 across.
explanation.walkthrough: '1 ac' looks like a cross-reference to 1 across (SHOCKWAVE, a cardiac shock), but it is read literally as I and AC.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearty in the literal sense of relating to the heart, which is what the medical word means.

clue.text: Following direction, head back to German city

parts.note: E is the compass point east, a direction

indicators.note: going back means the word is read in reverse

parts.note: a ness is a headland or promontory

explanation.surface: Instructions to follow, then head back to a German town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses NESS to SSEN; 'head' is a geographical headland, not a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: Essen is an industrial city in the Ruhr, in western Germany.

clue.text: Where to get hold of suckers with money a

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held and printed as 'Where to get hold of suckers with money a (5,4)': the scan shows it cut off after 'a', and no search finds the rest.
annotationWithheld.clue: Where to get hold of suckers with money a
